subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes transverse and longitudinal waves?
options: In transverse waves oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
In longitudinal waves oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer
In transverse waves oscillations are parallel to energy transfer
Both have oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer
questions.explain: Transverse waves oscillate perpendicular to the direction of energy travel, longitudinal waves oscillate parallel to it.

questions.q: Light travels from a medium of refractive index 1.5 toward air. The critical angle for total internal reflection is approximately:
A diffraction grating equation is d sinθ = nλ. For a grating with 300 lines per mm, the slit spacing d is:
In a Young's double-slit experiment the fringe spacing w is given by w = λD/s. To increase the fringe spacing you could:
questions.explain: Since w = λD/s, longer wavelength (smaller frequency) increases the fringe spacing.

questions.q: For a pipe closed at one end, the fundamental frequency forms a stationary wave with:
options: An antinode at the open end and node at the closed end
A node at the open end and antinode at the closed end
questions.explain: At a closed end air cannot move so a node forms; at an open end an antinode forms.

questions.q: The y-intercept of a maximum-KE-versus-frequency graph for the photoelectric effect equals:
questions.explain: From KEmax = hf − φ, the intercept on the KE axis is −φ (negative of the work function).

questions.q: A line emission spectrum consists of discrete coloured lines because:
options: Atomic electrons occupy only discrete energy levels
questions.explain: Discrete spectral lines arise because electrons occupy quantised energy levels, so only specific photon energies are emitted.

questions.q: Monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm strikes a grating with d = 2.0 × 10⁻⁶ m. At what angle does the first-order maximum appear?
An electron drops from an energy level of −1.5 eV to −3.4 eV. The energy of the emitted photon is:
questions.explain: Photon energy = |E_final − E_initial| = |−3.4 − (−1.5)| = 1.9 eV.

questions.q: A stationary wave is formed on a string fixed at both ends. The distance between adjacent nodes is:
questions.explain: Adjacent nodes (or antinodes) on a stationary wave are separated by half a wavelength.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by the wave model of light mainly because the wave model predicts:
options: Instant emission at all frequencies given enough intensity
questions.explain: The wave model predicts any frequency could eventually free electrons with enough intensity/time, contradicting the observed threshold frequency.

questions.q: When a wave refracts on entering a denser medium, which quantity stays constant?
questions.explain: Frequency is determined by the source and is unchanged on refraction; speed and wavelength both decrease.

questions.q: An electron has momentum 3.3 × 10⁻²⁴ kg m/s. Its de Broglie wavelength is (h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s):
Two points on a wave are separated by a path difference of one full wavelength. What is their phase difference?
questions.explain: One whole wavelength corresponds to a phase difference of 360° (2π radians).

questions.q: The work function of a metal is the:
options: Kinetic energy of the fastest electron
Minimum energy needed to release an electron from the metal surface
questions.explain: The work function φ is the minimum energy required to liberate an electron from the metal's surface.

questions.q: Light below the threshold frequency, however intense, produces no photoelectrons. This is best explained because:
options: Intensity does not affect electron emission
Each electron absorbs many photons at once
Each electron interacts with a single photon whose energy is too small
questions.explain: One electron absorbs one photon; if that single photon's energy hf is below φ, no electron is emitted regardless of intensity.

questions.q: If the speed of an electron is increased, its de Broglie wavelength:
questions.explain: Since λ = h/p and p = mv, increasing speed increases momentum and therefore decreases the wavelength.

questions.q: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on:
options: The intensity of the incident light
The frequency of the incident light
The size of the metal plate
questions.explain: Max KE = hf − φ, so it depends on the frequency of the light, not the intensity.

questions.q: In an electron diffraction tube, increasing the accelerating voltage causes the diffraction rings to:
questions.explain: Higher voltage gives electrons greater momentum and shorter de Broglie wavelength, so the diffraction rings shrink.

questions.q: When light reflects off the surface of water, the reflected light becomes partially polarised. This demonstrates that light is:
questions.explain: Only transverse waves can be polarised, so polarisation on reflection confirms light is transverse.

questions.q: In a photoelectric experiment, the stopping potential V_s relates to maximum KE by:
questions.explain: The stopping potential just halts the fastest electrons, so eV_s = ½mv²max, the maximum kinetic energy.

questions.q: Which harmonics are present in a pipe closed at one end?
questions.explain: A closed pipe supports only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th...) because of the node-antinode boundary conditions.

questions.q: Unpolarised light passes through two polarising filters whose transmission axes are at 90° to each other. The emergent intensity is:
questions.explain: Crossed polarisers (axes at 90°) block all the light, giving zero transmitted intensity.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by:
questions.explain: The de Broglie wavelength is λ = h/p, where p is the particle's momentum.

questions.q: White light passed through a diffraction grating produces spectra because:
options: Longer wavelengths diffract more than shorter ones
All wavelengths diffract by the same angle
Shorter wavelengths diffract more than longer ones
questions.explain: Since d sinθ = nλ, longer wavelengths (red) are diffracted through larger angles than shorter (violet).

questions.q: The de Broglie hypothesis applies to:
options: All moving particles, though the effect is significant only for very small masses
questions.explain: All moving matter has a de Broglie wavelength λ = h/p, but it is only measurable for tiny masses like electrons.

questions.q: Which property is unique to transverse waves and cannot occur with longitudinal waves?
questions.explain: Polarisation requires oscillations perpendicular to propagation, so only transverse waves can be polarised.

questions.q: The double-slit experiment provided important evidence that light:
options: Behaves as a wave because it produces interference fringes
questions.explain: The interference fringes can only be explained by superposition of waves, supporting the wave nature of light.

questions.q: How many photons of wavelength 600 nm are needed to deliver 1.0 J of energy? (E ≈ 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per photon)
questions.explain: Number = total energy / photon energy = 1.0 / 3.3×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ 3.0×10¹⁸ photons.
